back_translation: As dead flies make the perfumer's fragrant oil turn rancid, so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.
The heart of the wise inclines to the right, but the heart of the fool inclines to the left.
Even when the fool walks along the road, his sense is lacking, and he shows everyone that he is a fool.
If the ruler's anger rises against you, do not abandon your place, for calm composure can lay great offenses to rest.
There is an evil I have seen under the sun, like an inadvertent error that goes out from the one in power:
Folly is set in many high positions, while the rich sit in lowly places.
I have seen slaves on horseback, while nobles walk on the ground like slaves.
He who digs a pit may fall into it, and he who breaks through a fence may be bitten by a snake.
He who quarries stones may be hurt by them, and he who splits logs may be endangered by them.
If the axe is dull and its edge unsharpened, more strength must be exerted, but wisdom has the advantage of bringing success.
If the snake bites before it is charmed, the snake charmer gains no advantage.
The words from the mouth of the wise bring favor, but the lips of a fool swallow him up.
The words of his mouth begin with folly and end with wicked madness.
Yet the fool keeps multiplying words. Man does not know what will happen — who can tell him what will come after him?
The toil of fools wearies him, so that he does not even know the way into the city.
Woe to you, O land whose king is a child, and whose princes feast in the morning.
Happy are you, O land whose king is a son of nobles, and whose princes eat at the proper time — for strength and not for drunkenness.
Through laziness the roof sinks in, and through idle hands the house leaks.
A feast is made for laughter, wine makes life merry, and money answers everything.
Do not curse the king even in your thoughts, and do not curse the rich even in your bedroom, for a bird of the air may carry the sound, and a winged creature may report the matter.
